text: Which statement correctly contrasts the Reck (1994) and Clements (2016) decompositions of an N x N unitary?
choices: Reck's mesh is rectangular with depth N; Clements' is triangular with depth 2N-3
Both require N^2 MZIs but differ only in operating wavelength
Clements uses far fewer MZIs than Reck for the same unitary
Reck's is a triangular mesh (depth 2N-3, 1994); Clements' is a rectangular mesh (depth N, 2016) with balanced path lengths, now the standard
explanation: Both use the same N(N-1)/2 MZIs, but Clements' rectangular layout roughly halves the depth to N (vs Reck's 2N-3) and balances path lengths, reducing loss imbalance, which is why it is the modern standard. Option 0 swaps the two geometries, option 2 wrongly claims a different device count, and option 1 is wrong about both the count and the role of wavelength.
